items.headline: CAPE Phase 3 Confirmed for Late July - Finally Liquidated Entries
items.summary: CBP confirmed at the June 9 CIT hearing that CAPE Phase 3 will be ready by end of July 2026, covering finally liquidated entries that paid IEEPA tariffs. However, the DOJ continues to contest the legal authority to refund these entries without individual lawsuits, creating uncertainty about actual refund disbursements.

items.headline: CAPE Phase 2 Launch Date Set for June 29 - Reconciliation Entries
items.summary: CBP told the CIT on June 9 that CAPE Phase 2 will launch June 29, 2026, expanding functionality to process reconciliation entries. This represents approximately $28.7 billion in additional refunds. Over 16 million entries have been processed through Phase 1 with $89 billion accepted for processing.

items.headline: CBP Officials Testify on Refund Progress - $24 Billion Sent to Treasury
items.summary: At the June 9 CIT hearing, CBP Executive Assistant Commissioner Susan Thomas testified instead of Commissioner Scott after Federal Circuit intervention. CBP reported nearly $24 billion in refunds sent to Treasury for payment, with $480 million more expected this week. The agency expects to surpass $60 billion by month-end.

items.headline: Trump Administration Formally Appeals Universal Refund Order
items.summary: DOJ filed formal appeal at Federal Circuit challenging CIT's universal injunction requiring $166 billion in IEEPA refunds for non-litigants. The appeal specifically targets refunds for finally liquidated entries where importers haven't filed individual lawsuits, potentially blocking access for thousands of importers.

items.headline: CBP Reverses Position - Claims No Authority for Final Liquidations
items.summary: For the first time since the Supreme Court ruling, CBP asserted it lacks legal authority to refund finally liquidated entries (180+ days past liquidation) without importer-specific court orders. This position reversal affects the largest category of IEEPA refunds and signals intensifying government resistance.

items.headline: First ACH Payments Hit Importer Bank Accounts
items.summary: IEEPA tariff refunds began arriving in importer bank accounts via ACH transfer, marking the first successful completions of the CAPE Phase 1 process. CBP confirmed ACH payments could begin as early as May 12, with refunds typically taking 60-90 days from CAPE Declaration acceptance to disbursement.
